posts.title: What we record before the strip-out
posts.excerpt: Before building fabric is stripped out following escape of water or fire damage, our adjusters capture systematic moisture readings, photographs, and inventory records to establish an indisputable baseline of the loss.
posts.content:
When water escapes from a burst pipe or a fire is extinguished, the initial instinct on site is often to tear out damp materials immediately. Contractors arrive with demolition bars, carpets are pulled from grippers, and saturated plasterboard is dumped into skips before its condition is systematically documented. While rapid mitigation is understandable, premature demolition destroys the physical evidence required to assess cause, verify extent, and establish a clear baseline of damage. At Satei Adjusters, our independent desk in Bristol adheres to a calm and rigorous standard: record the property thoroughly before any strip-out begins. Preserving the undisturbed scene protects both the policyholder's history and the insurer's investigation.

When Ruth Abernethy confirms an appointment at our Bristol desk, an adjuster attends the property within 48 working hours. Before a single floorboard is lifted or a wall opened, our adjusters begin with non-destructive diagnostics. Tomás Ferreira and Samir Haddad employ calibrated pin and non-invasive moisture meters alongside thermal imaging cameras to track the true perimeter of moisture migration. Water frequently travels beneath laminates and behind drylining without visible surface staining. By taking systematic moisture readings across unaffected areas as well as saturated zones, we record the exact boundary of moisture penetration before drying contractors deploy desiccant equipment or air movers.

Simultaneously, we establish a comprehensive photographic record. Every room is documented from wide contextual angles down to close-up shots of tide marks, buckled floor joints, and soot deposition on structural timbers. We complete a structured room-by-room damage sheet that notes the material specification, age, and extent of compromise across every surface. Crucially, we also photograph adjacent unaffected rooms. Demonstrating where damage stops is just as critical for claims handlers as showing where it begins, eliminating future disputes over whether pre-existing wear or unrelated dampness formed part of the insured event.

Where personal effects, furnishings, or commercial stock are involved, Jonas Pike conducts an in-situ contents inventory before anything is moved or discarded. Items are tagged, photographed where they sit, and itemized with serial numbers, model details, and observable damage descriptions. In fire and smoke losses, such as the flat above a bakery in Cardiff where Jonas catalogued 212 items alongside Amara Nwosu, distinguishing between soot-contaminated items suitable for specialist cleaning and contents requiring replacement depends entirely on records taken before items are handled or transported.

Once our site attendance concludes, all field notes, moisture logs, and photographic registers return to our Canal Wharf desk. Lin Qiao reviews the technical evidence and edits the file into our standardized written report. Because our team records physical conditions methodically prior to strip-out, the appointing insurer receives an objective, uncompromised technical report within 5 working days of our site inspection. This disciplined baseline gives claims handlers total clarity to authorize appropriate structural drying, schedule necessary reinstatement, and reach fair claim resolutions without delay. Clear facts, established before alteration, protect the integrity of every subsequent claim decision.
